workload.description: One capability file in the project. 160 is a large application's worth of capabilities; 640 a large monorepo's. The ladder stops at 2,560, not 10,240, because every size writes a real project of TypeScript files and links them with the TypeScript compiler API, which takes minutes at the largest sizes.

notBenchmarked.buildChangeModel: Its input is the change report of the previous manifest, empty on a first run and small on any later one; the model it builds is derived once in the evidence build, which `build-evidence-model` measures.
notBenchmarked.buildCitationSnapshots: It re-reads the files that dynamic-access citations point at, and the fixtures declare no citations, so there is nothing for it to read at any size.
notBenchmarked.evaluateLiteral: An internal step of the parser that evaluates one syntax node of a schema literal, a constant amount of work per node; `parse-capability-file` measures it inside every parse.
notBenchmarked.generateUsage: It scans the files that consume the capabilities, and the fixtures contain none, so there is nothing for it to scan; the report it renders is measured as `render-usage-report`.
notBenchmarked.generatedBanner: It joins three short strings into one comment, a constant amount of work done once per generated file.
notBenchmarked.groupEdgesByCapability: It groups the dependency edges by capability, and the fixtures have no consumers, so there are no edges to group at any size.
notBenchmarked.groupEdgesByConsumer: It groups the dependency edges by consumer, and the fixtures have no consumers, so there are no edges to group at any size.
notBenchmarked.locationOf: It reads the position fields of one finding and builds one location, a constant amount of work done once per finding.
notBenchmarked.positionOf: It converts one syntax node's offset into a line and column, a constant amount of work done once per node.
notBenchmarked.renderCapabilityDiagram: It draws one diagram from the flows between capabilities and their consumers, and the fixtures have no consumers, so there are no flows to draw.
notBenchmarked.renderDependencyGraphDot: It draws the consumer graph, and the fixtures have no consumers, so the graph has no edges at any size.
notBenchmarked.renderOverviewDiagram: It draws one diagram from the flows between capabilities and their consumers, and the fixtures have no consumers, so there are no flows to draw.
notBenchmarked.renderSensitivityDiagram: It draws one diagram from the flows between capabilities and their consumers, and the fixtures have no consumers, so there are no flows to draw.
notBenchmarked.scanDependencies: It reads the files that consume the capabilities, and the fixtures contain none, so there is nothing for it to read at any size.
notBenchmarked.scanFileForUsage: An internal step of `scanDependencies` that reads one parsed consuming file; the fixtures contain no consuming files.
notBenchmarked.verifyDynamicAccessCitations: It verifies the files that dynamic-access citations point at, and the fixtures declare no citations, so there is nothing for it to verify.
notBenchmarked.writeEvidenceFingerprint: It writes one short text file through the filesystem adapter, which the standard keeps out of the benchmarks (no real I/O).
